title: A look at web frameworks: Quarkus, Javalin, Play and Micronaut

videos.script: Lesson 7 left you with a Spring Boot service that answers in problem details. {{bookshop}} Spring is not the only way to write that service in Java. Four other names turn up in job adverts and in older code: Quarkus, Micronaut, Javalin and Play. {{names}} They differ less in how a route looks than in when the application is wired. Spring works out its objects every time it starts. {{start}} Quarkus does that work during the build. Micronaut does it while compiling. Javalin leaves it to you, in your own main method. And Play, which comes from Scala, does it at start, like Spring. {{axis}} In this lesson you place each of them on that line, and see where you are likely to meet it. Then you build a small Javalin service by hand. {{javalin}} Last, you put it beside the bookshop and measure two things. How big each jar is, and how long each takes to answer its first request. {{measure}} The numbers will not choose a framework for you. They tell you what Spring's ecosystem costs, so you can decide when it is worth it. {{choice}}
